ambiguities.description: Optionality of Student-Offering enrollment: It is stated that 'students enroll in course offerings' and that 'a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in'. However, the transcript does not explicitly clarify whether every enrolled student must receive a grade, or conversely, whether grades are only issued for certain offerings or under certain conditions. The 'Student receives Grade for Offering' fact type requires both Student and Offering roles to be mandatory, but it is unclear from the transcript whether this is universally required or only for cases where enrollment occurred and the semester ended.

At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in. A student gets at most one grade per offering.

ambiguities.description: Instructor frequency constraint: The transcript states 'an instructor can teach several offerings in the same semester', which indicates that one instructor can teach multiple offerings per semester. However, the transcript does not specify an upper bound on how many offerings an instructor can teach, nor does it specify a minimum (e.g., can an instructor teach zero offerings?). The reverse constraint is also unclear: must every offering have an instructor, or can it be unassigned? The fact type captures the mandatory and uniqueness constraints, but the frequency bounds on instructors are not explicit.

source_references.excerpt: An instructor can teach several offerings in the same semester.

ambiguities.description: Course offering multiplicity: The transcript confirms that 'the same course can have multiple offerings', but does not specify whether a course must have at least one offering. It also does not specify an upper bound on the number of offerings per course or per semester. This affects cardinality constraints on the 'Offering is of Course' and 'Offering is in Semester' fact types.

source_references.excerpt: So the same course can have multiple offerings? Right. Each offering is of exactly one course and belongs to exactly one semester.

ambiguities.description: Capacity enforcement: The transcript states that each offering 'has a maximum capacity -- a cap on how many students can enroll'. However, it does not clarify whether the system enforces this cap (e.g., rejecting enrollments beyond capacity) or merely tracks it for reporting purposes. This affects whether a constraint on 'Student enrolls in Offering' cardinality (limited by Capacity) should be modeled.

source_references.excerpt: Each offering has a maximum capacity -- a cap on how many students can enroll.

ambiguities.description: Objectification necessity: The model includes 'Enrollment' as an objectified entity type derived from 'Student enrolls in Offering', based on the fact that grades are assigned to enrollments. However, the transcript does not explicitly name 'Enrollment' or state that it is tracked as a separate entity with its own identifier. The objectification is inferred from the semantic need to associate grades with specific student-offering pairs, but it remains unclear whether the system should expose Enrollment as a first-class entity with its own enrollment ID or whether grades should be modeled directly on the binary relationship.

source_references.excerpt: At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in.

ambiguities.description: Temporal scope of 'teaches': The transcript states 'each offering is taught by exactly one instructor' but does not clarify whether this is the current instructor assignment or a historical record. If an offering can change instructors over time, or if the model should track past instructors, this constraint may need to be refined. Similarly, the temporal scope of 'enrolls' and 'receives grade' is not specified.

source_references.excerpt: Each offering is taught by exactly one instructor.

ambiguities.description: Semester date ordering: The transcript states that 'a semester has a start date and an end date' but does not specify whether the end date must be after the start date. This is a domain constraint that may need to be explicitly modeled.

source_references.excerpt: A semester has a start date and an end date.

ambiguities.description: Grade mandatory for all enrollments: The phrase 'a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in' could be interpreted as: (1) every enrollment must eventually yield a grade, or (2) only students who complete the offering receive a grade. The transcript does not clarify whether a student can enroll without ultimately receiving a grade (e.g., due to withdrawal or incomplete status). This affects whether 'Student receives Grade for Offering' should have a mandatory constraint on both roles or only on one.
